evidence.captureCoverageWarning: The r51 packet omits the contract-requested 135-degree and 225-degree views plus dedicated arena-close and rear-close captures. The supplied orbit, clay and phone views still expose the decisive honey-dipper and phone failures.

source-identity.evidence: The authoritative icon is two unmistakable crossed golden honey dippers. The arena is visible, but its crossed objects read as black construction bars with an orange central block; the source's defining nectar-trial emblem is not preserved.

arena-silhouette.evidence: The circular/radial platform, front stairs, open contest floor and low crown establish a plausible arena silhouette without a heavy roof hiding the floor. This is the blockout's strongest dimension.

honey-dipper-readability.evidence: In the clearest 045-degree evidence the crossed forms have thick dark shafts and a block-like orange joint/head. Slender handles, two distinct ribbed cylindrical honey heads, grooved texture and restrained hanging drops are not visibly readable; they look like hammers or crossed beams.

surface-depth.evidence: The platform, columns, crown and stairs have real volumetric depth and the central floor is open. The emblem itself lacks the modeled head/handle depth needed to read as the source object, and the nectar core is not clearly resolved.

arcade-continuity.evidence: Columns and the low circular crown form a coherent open arcade through the available orbit, with plausible roof support and no obvious disappearing bay. Some views still read as a generic rotunda because the arena emblem is weak.

side-rear-continuity.evidence: The 090/180/270/315 views preserve the open arcade and supported ring, but no clear secondary crossed-honey-dipper silhouette survives around the side or rear. The architecture continues; the Nectar Trials identity does not.

phone-readability.evidence: In phone-overview the arena is clipped against the right edge and only part of its crown is visible. Neither the crossed emblem nor honey-dipper heads can be identified, so the landmark does not communicate its source identity at intended scale.

strictRejects.rule: block hammers, axes, or generic construction tools
strictRejects.evidence: The crossed dark bars with orange block-like ends/joint read as hammers or structural beams rather than two grooved honey dippers.
The crown is predominantly honey-gold and purple remains limited to subordinate banners.
The platform and stairs provide arena cues, but the failed dipper emblem leaves several oblique views reading as a generic open rotunda.

strictRejects.rule: oversized roof ring hiding the contest floor
strictRejects.evidence: The open contest floor remains visible in 000/045/090.
The crossed elements appear physically attached to the dais/crown system rather than floating independently.
No readable secondary crossed-dipper silhouette survives the 180 and 270 views.
The arcade and crown continue coherently around the rear even though landmark identity does not.

gauntletAction.reason: The first blockout triggers the explicit block-hammer and front-only-emblem rejects, while honey-dipper readability and phone readability fall below the 0.50 critical floor. Gauntlet economics therefore prohibit spending the bounded correction on this construction family.

dominantDefect: The defining crossed honey dippers are represented as thick dark construction bars with block-like orange centers, so the otherwise coherent arena shell loses the source's identity in desktop, side/rear and phone views.
